name: truedone
description:
truedone checks whether a pull request's tests prove its change: red without the change, green with it. It also flags tests that were skipped, focused or weakened. Each pull request gets one verdict, as a check run and a label, so you see what the tests show before you read the diff.

**On each pull request**

- A check run named truedone, with the verdict and the reason for it.
- One label: `truedone:yes`, `truedone:weak`, `truedone:tampered`, `truedone:review`, `truedone:no-evidence`, `truedone:unrun`, `truedone:pending` or `truedone:could-not-run`. A pull request with nothing to check gets none.

**Why each permission**

- Pull requests, write: read the changed files and set the label.
- Checks, write: post the check run.
- Contents, read: read each changed test at the base and at the head.
- Actions, read: read the report the truedone action uploads, for the red-green verdict.
- Metadata, read: GitHub requires it.

It never runs your code. The static checks only read files. The red-green run happens in your own workflow, through the truedone action.

**To turn it off** for one repository, add `enabled: false` to `.github/truedone.yml` on your default branch, or uninstall the app.

This is a preview. [truedone.pages.dev](https://truedone.pages.dev) shows what works today. Source: [github.com/mgillr/truedone](https://github.com/mgillr/truedone) (Apache-2.0). [Privacy](https://truedone.pages.dev/privacy) and [terms](https://truedone.pages.dev/terms).
